pages.text: Chance has laws. Repeat an experiment n times, each a success with probability p, and exactly k successes happen with probability C(n,k)·p^k·(1 − p)^(n−k). Three heads in ten tosses: 11.7%.
Roll the $(item)Dice Set$() and add them: seven comes up a sixth of the time, two and twelve one time in thirty-six each.

$(thing)Combinatorics$() counts without listing. There are n! ways to order n things, and for large n, ln n! ≈ n ln n − n. The $(item)Quantum Random Number Chip$() draws its bits from single photons at a half-silvered mirror - the only randomness nothing can predict.
